rules: The link is inline text inside its context: arrange label, meta and indicator in that order inside container. It takes the font family, size, weight and line height of the surrounding text; it sets no typography of its own.

destination tells the reader what the link leads to before they follow it. page (default): another page of the product, opened in the same context, with no meta and no indicator. external: a page outside the product, opened in a new browsing context without access to the opener. email: an email address (href is a mailto: address). phone: a phone number (href is a tel: number). file: a document or a file. print: a printable version of the current content (opening the print dialog is an action, not a link).

indicator shows one glyph of the reference icon set, one em square, after indicatorGap: external an up-right arrow, email an envelope, phone a handset, print a printer, file the glyph of fileType (below); page shows none. The glyph is decorative and never underlined: a subtle complement drawn in indicatorColor with tone accent, and in the inherited context color at inheritIndicatorOpacity with tone inherit.

File glyphs by fileType, matched ignoring case and a leading dot: pdf a PDF file; doc, docx, odt, rtf a text document; xls, xlsx, ods a spreadsheet; csv a CSV file; ppt, pptx, odp a presentation; txt, md a plain text file; zip, rar, 7z, gz, tar an archive; png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, svg an image; mp3, wav, ogg an audio file; mp4, mov, webm a video; any other value, or no fileType, a generic file.

With destination file, meta shows the format and the size as visible text in parentheses after the label: fileType in uppercase without its dot, then fileSize as given, separated by a comma ((PDF, 2.4 MB)); a missing value is left out, and meta is absent when both are. meta is a subtle complement in metaColor with tone accent and in the inherited context color with tone inherit, is not underlined and is part of the accessible name. The component neither formats sizes nor forces a download.

The accessible name is label, then meta, then the announced suffix of the destination: external opens in a new tab, email email, phone phone, print printable version; page and file have none. A non-empty destinationLabel replaces the default suffix (translation).

The label is underlined in every state, so that a link is never identified by color alone. The underline is underlineWidth thick by default and underlineHoverWidth when hovered or pressed; the color does not change between interaction states, and visited links look the same as unvisited ones.

With tone accent the label and its underline are drawn in content; with tone inherit they take the content color of the surrounding text, for colored contexts (a status message, an inverse surface) where the accent color would not reach the required contrast. Meta and indicator follow the two rules above, so that only the underlined words read as the link.
Inside a sentence the label wraps like the surrounding text; meta and indicator stay attached to the last word and never start a line alone.
The link has no disabled state: a destination that cannot be followed is shown as plain text.
When focus is true and was reached by keyboard, draw a focus indicator of focusWidth in focusColor at focusOffset around each line box of the link, with corners of focusRadius.
The underline thickness change is immediate; there is no animation.
In forced-colors mode the link, its meta and its indicator use the system link color, the underline stays and the focus indicator stays visible.
A host whose text carries its own color (an Alert) may ask its links to inherit: a link that does not set tone then takes tone inherit. An explicit tone always wins.
